body:
Grace Kim: seeing a correctness issue w/ selector v2 on canary. One of the attention kernels is producing NaNs for a specific shape bucket. Not 100% repro yet but I can hit it locally w/ the lab config. Flagging bc we need a conformance test + probably mark this kernel unsafe for that regime.

Grace Kim: details so far:
- model: Llama-ish (GQA enabled) fp16
- regime: prefill, long context (4k+) w/ smaller batch
- GPU: A10 (SM86) in benchmark-lab
- selected kernel: `flash_attn_v3_sm80` (via compat path)
- symptom: output logits contain NaNs after ~2-3 steps; then sampling goes off the rails

Sana Farid: :eyes: do we have any traces / selector explain output confirming the kernel id + inputs? want to make sure it’s not the telemetry label lying.

Grace Kim: yeah, grabbed from the trace annotation (`kernel_choice`) + also from debug print.

Grace Kim:
```
selector=v2 model_family=llama_gqa seq_bucket=prefill_long gpu=a10
kernel_id=flash_attn_v3_sm80
reason=table_match
shape: b=2 q_len=4096 kv_len=4096 n_heads=32 n_kv_heads=8 head_dim=128 dtype=fp16
post_check: logits_nan=true at token=0
```

Omar El-Sayed: token=0 NaN during prefill is extra sus. are we sure it’s not the softmax mask / causal mask path? did this only happen after wiring the scheduler prefill/decode split?

Grace Kim: first noticed after the seq-bucket plumbing landed, but I think it just made it easier to hit the “prefill_long” entry on A10. v1 used to fall back to the older kernel there.

Yuki Sato: A10 running the sm80 kernel smells like we’re going through a “generic” build w/ assumptions that don’t hold on sm86. we probably should not route A10 -> sm80 v3 for long q_len.

Yuki Sato: quick q: is this kernel actually compiled for sm86 or are we using PTX JIT? if it’s JIT’ing, numeric differences + uninitialized shared mem bugs can show up.

Grace Kim: looks like PTX JIT path (from verbose logs). I’ll paste the relevant line.

Grace Kim:
```
[attn] flash_v3: cubin missing for sm86, using ptx fallback (sm80)
```

Hiro Tanaka: ok we should treat that as unsafe until proven otherwise. can we pin A10 prefill_long to the “safe set” kernel (v2 table override) as a stopgap?

Noah Patel: +1. Also: we need a regression test that would have caught this. Conformance test should explicitly check for NaNs + compare against reference within tolerance, across the selector’s buckets.

Anika Gupta: I can add a conformance case for that exact shape and run it across A10/A100/H100 in CI (or at least nightly). Do we have a minimal repro script + seed so it’s deterministic?

Grace Kim: I can make it deterministic (fixed input activations + fixed weights). The current repro is running a full model forward; but we can isolate the attention op w/ synthetic tensors.

Marcus Reed: if we isolate to the attention op, we can add it to the kernel conformance suite rather than the full perf harness. That’s probably the right place.

ci-bot: Buildkite: `runtime-conformance` (branch `selector-v2-canary`) failed: NaN detected in `attn_forward` for test `llama_gqa_prefill_long_a10` (new)

Anika Gupta: lol ok that was fast. Grace did you already push a WIP test?

Grace Kim: I hacked one in my branch to see if it’d light up. It fails on A10 runner, passes on A100 runner.

Omar El-Sayed: that lines up w/ the PTX fallback suspicion. We should also make selector v2 treat “no native cubin for this GPU” as an incompatibility signal (so it won’t pick it even if table says so).

Yuki Sato: +1. Kernel registry should have `supported_sms` or `requires_cubin=true` so selection can gate. Otherwise we’ll keep stepping on these.

Hiro Tanaka: for immediate mitigation: update selection matrix so A10 + prefill_long -> `flash_attn_v2_sm86_safe` (whatever we call it) and mark `flash_attn_v3_sm80` disallowed on sm86.

Grace Kim: ack. I’ll send a small config/registry change PR today. For the longer-term, we can plumb `native_binary_available` into the selection context.

Noah Patel: keep it simple for now: allowlist kernel ids by gpu_sku (normalized) rather than “sm version” only. we already have SKU normalization work ongoing.

Sana Farid: rollout implication: if this is in canary, we should add a guardrail alert for `nan_detected` tagged by `kernel_id` so we catch it before customers do. (even if we sample it)

Marcus Reed: we already have `runtime.nan_guard` metric in a couple places but not broken down by kernel. adding a low-cardinality breakdown might be ok if we bucket kernel id.

Anika Gupta: for conformance suite:
- test should fail on any NaN/Inf in output
- compare against reference attention implementation (torch) for a small tolerance (fp16)
- run for a matrix of: head_dim {128}, q_len {4096}, kv_len {4096}, gqa {true}, batch {1,2}
- gate: kernel must either pass or be excluded by selector constraints

Grace Kim: sounds good. I’ll file it under ENG-3928 and link the failing shape + kernel id.

Yuki Sato: can someone double-check if `flash_attn_v3_sm80` is even supposed to be used on anything except A100/H100 paths? we might be over-sharing it.

Hiro Tanaka: it was intended for sm80+ but only when we have cubins for that SM. PTX fallback was never validated. let’s codify that.

Omar El-Sayed: action items:
1) Grace: registry/table update to avoid selecting this on A10 prefill_long (today)
2) Anika: add conformance test + NaN guard (this week)
3) Yuki: add selector constraint: don’t choose kernels without native cubin (or explicit allow) (follow-up)

Grace Kim: :thumbsup: will do. I’ll also add an "unsafe_kernel" entry so we can hotfix via config if this pops up elsewhere.

Sana Farid: please also paste the kernel id + shape into the perf canary notes so SRE knows what to watch for when we re-enable.

Anika Gupta: once the conformance test lands, we should also make sure the selector v2 table PR can’t add a kernel for a bucket without a corresponding conformance coverage entry (even if it’s just a lightweight check).

Noah Patel: love that. registry lint: “every kernel_id referenced in v2 table must have conformance metadata + last_known_good commit hash”

Grace Kim: ok, I’ll keep the first PR minimal and we can iterate on the registry schema. Linking WIP PR soon.
